title: ReplicateBE.jl cannot represent a negative subject-by-formulation correlation, which FDA's FA0(2) permits
raised_by: PR #62, first gating run of the nine synthetic full-replicate cases
effect_on_be_stats: none on any computed value. It bounds where the tier-3 oracle is usable: two of the nine synthetic cases are excluded from the comparison, by a criterion measured from the oracle's own reported parameters rather than from whether the comparison passed.

what_was_observed.agreeing_cases: Seven of nine agree to 1e-6 on all five covariance parameters, on the standard error and on the denominator df.
what_was_observed.the_pattern: The two disagreeing cases are EXACTLY the two where be-stats fits a negative subject-by-formulation correlation. Every case with rho >= 0 agrees. No other property separates them - B is unbalanced and incomplete, D is balanced and complete.

what_this_is_and_is_not.it_is_not: Evidence of a be-stats defect. No production number changed as a result of this finding, and none should.

the_three_models_stated_separately.fda_appendix_c: TYPE=FA0(2) is G = LL' with L = [[l11, 0], [l21, l22]], so sigma_BTBR = l11*l21. l21 is UNCONSTRAINED IN SIGN, therefore a negative subject-by-formulation covariance is PERMITTED by the model FDA specifies - as it is under the CSH and UNR alternatives FDA names as acceptable substitutes.
the_three_models_stated_separately.be_stats: Implements that parameterisation directly, and CAN FIT a negative covariance. It does so on cases B and D.
the_three_models_stated_separately.replicatebe_jl_1_0_15: Parameterises the correlation through a link, `rholink = :psigmoid`, whose range EXCLUDES NEGATIVE VALUES. Reaching zero requires sending its parameter to minus infinity, and 1e-14 is what the optimiser returns when it tries. Those values are not small numbers; they are zero as that link can express it. It CANNOT REPRESENT a negative correlation.
the_three_models_stated_separately.conclusion: In this region the two implementations are not fitting the same model: the oracle is fitting a constrained one. Its disagreement is therefore uninformative about be-stats, and it must not be treated as an adjudicating oracle there.

how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.route: The classical subject-level analysis - the one-sample analysis of per-subject (mean log T - mean log R) averaged over sequences. No mixed model, no REML, no optimiser, no covariance structure, no Satterthwaite formula.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.applies_to: Case D, which is balanced, complete and interior. PR #62 established that Appendix C reduces to this analysis exactly under those three conditions.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.reading: A third route sharing code with neither implementation agrees with be-stats to eight decimal places and differs from the oracle by 3.2%. Holding case D out of the gate therefore rests on a number rather than on a reading of ReplicateBE's source.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.evidence_class: Independent algebraic / structural cross-check, sharing no code with the REML implementation. Explicitly NOT tier 1A, which in this package means conformance to a regulator's stated algorithm or decision rule. No regulator states this identity.

case_b.why: Case B is INCOMPLETE, so the balanced-data identity does not apply to it, and ReplicateBE cannot represent its negative correlation. No independent check on this fit exists anywhere in this project.
case_b.what_is_NOT_claimed: That case B is externally validated. It is not. It is held out of the tier-3 gate for the same structural reason as case D and supported by none of the same evidence.
case_b.what_would_resolve_it: An oracle whose covariance parameterisation admits negative subject-by-formulation correlation AND which handles available-case missing data - or a SAS PROC MIXED run on this dataset.
case_b.enforced_by: tests/validation/test_appendix_c_case_oracle.py::test_case_b_has_no_independent_oracle_and_is_not_claimed_to, which asserts the three facts that make it unresolved so that a future change satisfying any of them surfaces as a failure rather than passing unnoticed.

what_was_not_done.no_tolerance_was_loosened: The gate is unchanged at 0.01 percentage points on each confidence limit. Widening it until B and D passed would have required about 0.6 percentage points, which would also have admitted a genuine defect.
what_was_not_done.no_case_was_dropped_for_disagreeing: The criterion is a conjunction of two measured properties - be-stats rho clearly below zero AND the oracle's rho collapsed below its link's limit - and a test asserts that exactly the cases meeting it fall outside the gate. A case where the oracle merely fitted a small positive correlation would still be compared.
what_was_not_done.no_case_was_deleted: Both remain in the suite, both are still fitted by the oracle in every CI run, and both are still reported.
what_was_not_done.the_criterion_is_reversible: If a future ReplicateBE release reported a negative rho, these cases would re-enter the gate automatically.

consequence: ReplicateBE.jl is a tier-3 implementation oracle WITHIN THE COVARIANCE DOMAIN IT CAN REPRESENT - fully replicate designs whose fitted subject-by-formulation correlation is non-negative. That covers EMA Data set I, the regulator-published case, and seven of the nine synthetic ones, and there the live comparison gates. It does not cover negative-correlation fits: there it is structurally fitting a different, constrained model, and it is neither an oracle nor evidence of a defect.
